chunks: It contains clear signs, the standing place of Abraham. And whoever enters it will be secure. And to God is due the pilgrimage of the House for whoever is able to undertake a journey to it. And whoever disbelieves, then God is independent of the worlds.

key_terms.مَقَامُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: The standing place of Prophet Abraham

ai.seo_question: What are the key elements of the Hajj obligation mentioned in Surah Aal-Imran?
ai.summary: This verse, known as the 'Verse of Hajj' (Ayat al-Hajj), establishes the fifth pillar of Islam by defining the conditions of capability (istita'ah) and the sanctity of the Kaaba, where entry guarantees safety (amān). In Shia tradition, the Maqam Ibrahim is revered not only as a physical site but as a spiritual station linking the legacy of Ibrahim and Ismail to the Imams, emphasizing the continuity of divine guidance. The concluding declaration of God's self-sufficiency (Ghani) underscores that the ritual is for human benefit, while the 'one who disbelieies' often refers to those who neglect the obligation despite ability.
